scenes.text: You probably think the dry, desolate Sahara desert and the lush, wet Amazon rainforest have absolutely nothing in common, but these two extremes are actually deeply connected partners.
Every single year, incredibly powerful windstorms howling over the African desert kick up millions of tons of yellow, nutrient-rich dust high into the atmosphere.

This massive cloud travels over three thousand miles across the Atlantic Ocean to fertilize the Amazon with phosphorus, a vital nutrient that the rainforest's heavy rains constantly wash away from the soil.

Without this mind-blowing African dust delivery, the entire Amazon rainforest would starve and slowly collapse, so drop a comment below if you already knew this and follow for more incredible science!
